comments.text: Actor type three starts at the player's position, cycles an eight-step horizontal wobble and moves upward one pixel per update. It remains visible only while its terrain sample is character $11-$14; leaving that range releases the slot. Initialization chooses the phase from CIA timer low bits, uses shape $A0 and colour one.
Operand byte 1 of the BPL instruction at $6C02, within the described level actor or raster routine. This name marks a patched operand rather than another routine entry.
Eight signed half-pixel X steps, indexed by the cyclic phase in $BC61,X. The vertical step is a separate DEC of actor Y.

Actor type four reserves five extra slots and builds a six-part body from the offset, state and colour arrays at $6E47-$6E5E. The main part starts with 64 health at $BCD6; terrain character damage and wheel contact subtract through the shared damage table. Death awards 5000 points and scatters all six parts into individually damageable fragments. A fragment awards 500 points before its normal explosion. Leaving the bounds frees the linked slots.
Clear the six slot types and X positions, restore each slot's default Y, then continue the shared actor scan.

Sample up to seven successive terrain rows across two columns beneath the main part. A character at least $C8 is replaced by $FF and converted into a damage-table index. Surviving hits flash all six parts white; death or the common kill flag scatters them.

Request 5000 score points and give all six components state two, shape $B0, colour eight and sixteen health. Load their horizontal and vertical fragment steps from the six-entry arrays; request two death effects.

State-two fragments accept player contact and character damage, award 500 points on destruction, and move by their saved signed X/Y steps. Bounds release the slot; a nonzero terrain property requests its explosion.
Six half-pixel horizontal offsets for the initial linked body.
Six pixel vertical offsets for the initial linked body.
Six initial states: the first component controls the group and the remaining components render it.
Six initial body colours, restored before testing the group's hit state.
Six signed horizontal steps assigned when the linked body scatters.
Six signed vertical steps assigned when the linked body scatters.

Actor type five starts with three health, faces the player and walks with four-frame animation. Terrain checks reverse it at walls and start a falling state when support disappears. Within thirty half-pixel units of the player it waits and periodically jumps using the vertical-step table. Damage flashes its colour; death or invulnerable/wheel contact awards 200 points.

Choose near-player waiting, grounded walking or falling. Side and floor property samples control facing and a thirteen-step falling curve; the near-player jump restarts with index fifteen. Bounds release the actor.
Decrement the thirty-update wait counter. Expiry starts a jump with vertical index fifteen; otherwise face the player and test whether their horizontal separation remains below thirty half-pixels.
Set state two if absolute player/actor X separation is below thirty, otherwise state zero. Save the direction toward the player only in the near state. Returns Y as the selected state.
Sixteen signed vertical increments, read with a decreasing index. Falling installs twelve; the near-player jump installs fifteen. Index zero remains selected after the decrement reaches zero.
Two facing-dependent base shape numbers, added to the four-frame walk index or selected directly at initialization.

Actor type six starts with ten health and waits fifty updates before flying toward the player's side with a selected vertical step. Surviving character hits can allocate a type-sixteen projectile with an X step matching its facing and a timer-selected Y step. Contact, character damage and the shared kill flag can destroy it for 150 points. Terrain contact requests its explosion.

If an actor slot is available, create the shared type-sixteen projectile five pixels below and four half-pixels to the right of this actor. Store signed X and timer-selected Y motion in the generated projectile arrays at $CB53/$CB5E.

Toggle the two-frame facing animation every four updates. State zero waits, then selects a vertical step from the player's relative height; state one adds the saved X/Y steps and tests terrain and bounds.
Two animation shape numbers for the first facing, selected every fourth update.
Two animation shape numbers for the other facing.
Two signed X steps, minus two and plus two, used by both this flyer and its emitted projectiles.
Eight overlapping signed Y-step bytes selected by the low three timer bits. The three-byte motion-choice table at $716D is a subrange of this allocation.
Three signed vertical steps selected when the fifty-update wait ends: minus one, zero or plus one according to the player's height.

Actor type seven reserves three additional slots, assigns four component offsets and starts a shared forty-point health counter at $BCDB. The controller samples a five-row character-damage span, flashes every component on a surviving hit and awards 1500 points on death. It drifts left where terrain permits and moves vertically toward the player, then copies the component offsets to all four sprites.

Derive screen row and column, then sample two adjacent characters in each of up to five rows. A character at least $C8 is erased and indexes the shared damage table. Surviving damage flashes all four colours white; underflow or the kill flag destroys all four parts.
Award 1500 points and set all four saved actor slots to the common explosion type/state.

Toggle selected component shapes on independent eight-update and three-update dividers. Try moving left, choose a vertical step toward the player's span, check terrain and update each component from the four saved offsets.
Clear each linked slot's type and X, then load its default Y byte and store that byte to X again. The second store is also to $7A,X; this code does not restore $85,X.
Four horizontal component offsets in half-pixels.
Four pixel Y offsets forming the upper and lower component pairs.
Four initial states, with the first slot controlling the linked group and the other three rendering it.
Four initial shape numbers for the linked body.

Actor type eight interprets its subtype as one of three colour/animation variants. It chooses signed horizontal and vertical steps toward the player's initial relative position, reflects those steps at solid terrain, and cycles the variant's shape sequence. Contact or a detected character hit destroys it for 150 points; variant two also emits timer-spaced projectiles. No health counter is subtracted on the detected hit path.

Sample the prospective horizontal and vertical edges. A solid property toggles signed X step with XOR $FE or signed Y step with XOR $FC, reversing the respective plus/minus one or plus/minus two motion.
Use the subtype-specific frame divider and maximum frame index. Variant zero and two select facing-dependent shape arrays, while variant one uses a single four-frame sequence.

Variant two periodically chooses a timer-based delay and allocates a type-sixteen shot. Timer-selected signed vertical motion is also used as the horizontal step after OR one; the shot starts at the actor plus its fixed offsets.
Three initial colours indexed by subtype zero through two.
Three initial shapes indexed by subtype.
Three animation divider reload values.
Last animation index for each subtype; indices count down and reload here.
Three signed direction choices, plus one, zero and minus one. The Y choice is doubled before storage.
Three frame shapes for the first direction of variant zero.
Three frame shapes for the other direction of variant zero.
Four frame shapes used by variant one.
Two frame shapes for the first direction of variant two.
Two frame shapes for the other direction of variant two.

Actor type ten starts in platform state fourteen with ten reward-count steps. A character hit changes it to state fifteen; later hits count down a five-hit divider, spawn reward actors and eventually destroy it for 5000 points. Player standing and underside contact update the shared platform flags. A triggered bump uses the nine-byte curve at $9C3A. Spawned rewards remain type ten while flying and become ordinary type-two pickups on terrain contact or after their motion curve.

The first hit changes the platform's shape and state. Subsequent hits flash it, count down the hit divider and decrement its reward counter; underflow clears platform flags and explodes it. Otherwise allocate a reward with timer-selected subtype and signed launch steps.

OR standing and underside flags across eleven platform slots into the shared flags. Apply any active bump curve, then compare the player's position against the platform's top and underside. Standing snaps player Y to the platform; a new underside bump advances its reward state.

Compute terrain pointers and reflect signed X motion at an edge or obstacle. Read the thirty-one-entry vertical curve at $A0E0; terrain or the final index converts the actor to a freshly initialized type-two pickup. The side selector reads $BC6C without X while the movement step reads $BC6C,X.

Actor type eleven attaches X to the player and starts at the saved surface Y. Subtype zero toggles its two shapes using an XOR divider; nonzero subtype starts sixteen pixels above the surface, requests a splash effect and advances through eight transient frames before releasing the slot.

Actor type twelve allows one active instance, records its slot and replaces the end-of-frame callback with $77C8. It adjusts the saved surface Y by the scrolling phase and selects shared multicolours above/below the surface. When the surface moves above the playfield, it restores the normal callback and clears the active flag.

Set the raster comparison to $D5, set both playfield multicolours, restore the saved next raster-handler vector and refresh the surface Y from its controlling actor. Return through the shared interrupt exit.

Shared initialization and per-update callback for this level. Reset surface state on player death, test the grounded right-side exit, choose location-dependent character animations, and replace the player movement hook while the sampled terrain character identifies water. Water entry adjusts weapon motion parameters; leaving water restores the saved player hook and can initiate an upward transition.

Advance the four-character water pattern on an eight-update divider. Near the active surface, allocate or remove the attached surface actor and start its splash delay. Then animate the separate single-character three-frame pattern on a five-update divider.

Rotate a two-character bitmap strip, shift adjacent double-width glyphs in opposite directions and copy two phase-selected glyph frames. Side terrain characters $66-$69 push player X by one half-pixel when adjacent terrain is passable and the opposing joystick direction is not held.

Rotate the two sixteen-byte glyph halves, then select one of nine low/high routine targets through the camera subphase at $19. The patched JMP chooses no extra rotation, a left rotate or a right rotate.
Operand byte 1 of the JMP instruction at $7AB3, within the described level actor or raster routine. This name marks a patched operand rather than another routine entry.
Operand byte 2 of the JMP instruction at $7AB3, within the described level actor or raster routine. This name marks a patched operand rather than another routine entry.
Rotate each of the sixteen paired glyph rows left through carry, then return through $7AC5.
Rotate each of the sixteen paired glyph rows right through carry.

Replace normal player movement on the water-character path. Set swimming weapon offsets and movement flags, sample fire, build the terrain pointer, periodically allocate rising effects, and scan eight joystick bit masks. A matching direction patches a JSR from the split tables at $9B26/$9B2E and selects a speed. With no direction, save the checkpoint and apply alternate-update vertical bobbing. Select the facing-dependent swimming shape before returning.
Operand byte 1 of the JSR instruction at $7B96, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.
Operand byte 2 of the JSR instruction at $7B96, within the described level routine. This address names an operand inside the instruction, rather than another routine entry.
Select upward motion and enter the common three-character vertical collision test.
Select downward motion and enter the common three-character vertical collision test. Only passable terrain and the corresponding Y bound permit motion by the saved speed.
Select left-facing motion and test four vertically stacked terrain characters. Passable terrain and the left bound permit decrementing half-pixel X.
Select right-facing motion and test four vertically stacked terrain characters. Passable terrain and the right bound permit incrementing half-pixel X.
Run leftward movement followed by upward movement.
Run rightward movement followed by upward movement.
Run leftward movement followed by downward movement.
Run rightward movement followed by downward movement.

Actor type fifteen waits for the grounded camera region, disables normal camera movement, clears other actors and installs the large-body raster/copy hooks. Its initial health is $0290, or 656 damage units, at $BCDE/$BCDF. The body has four columns of six bands. A thirty-entry action sequence chooses rise, descend, wait and flashing actions. Damage can switch it to a free-moving phase; final death creates explosions, restores hooks and awards 10000 points.

Clear actor and transient state, install the boss callbacks, set 656 health and derive four X coordinates and six Y coordinates from its source actor. Fill a twelve-character terrain strip with timer-selected characters, establish the body pose and patch its initial flashing cells.

When the prior action ends, use the next of thirty action IDs at $A09A to read split routine-address bytes from $96C4/$9704. Patch the JSR at $7DEA, advance/wrap the sequence and clear its initialization flag. The same update advances a twelve-character strip through $F1-$F3 on a three-update divider except in the free-moving phase.
Operand byte 1 of the JSR instruction at $7DEA, within the described level actor or raster routine. This name marks a patched operand rather than another routine entry.
Operand byte 2 of the JSR instruction at $7DEA, within the described level actor or raster routine. This name marks a patched operand rather than another routine entry.

On first entry load this action's duration and optionally select its body pose. Every other update decrement all six band Y coordinates until the duration expires, then end the action. Alternating sound requests mark movement and completion.
Select the moving pose on entry, then increment all six Y coordinates on alternate updates until its duration ends. Decrement the active action counter on completion.
Load the indexed action duration, choose the default pose when necessary, and count updates until the action ends.

Initialize duration, pose and a twenty-update wait. Toggle between the normal pose and patched flashing cells using delays at $96BE; each completed flash cycle decrements the action duration and eventually ends it.

During state $D4, move all four body X coordinates with signed direction, toggling high-X masks on wrap. Move the leading Y and derive the next two bands. Timer counters and bounds reverse motion; pause windows alternate body flashing and gradually increase horizontal speed up to eight.

Derive half-pixel boss X from its sprite X and high-X mask, clear the standing flag, and test four adjacent contact rectangles across the body top. The shared test permits standing in the nonnegative action phase and damages an unprotected player touching the body sides.
Operand byte 2 of the LDA instruction at $7FF3, within the described level actor or raster routine. This name marks a patched operand rather than another routine entry.

Compare the player against the supplied body rectangle. Standing snaps Y to the surface, rebuilds the player terrain pointer and removes this helper's caller return address. Other overlap can remove that return address and jump directly to player damage. This routine deliberately changes the return stack.

Derive terrain pointers from the body origin. Pose-selected offsets sample two possible pairs across seven rows. Character hits erase their source cell; $F1-$F3 are ignored. The active pose, sample row/side and standing state gate damage. Subtract through the shared damage table from the two-byte health counter; a high-byte transition starts component explosions and installs the free-motion action, while final underflow starts death.

During transition state $D3, animate six selected body cells on individual timer delays. Completed explosions hide the corresponding shape. Once all six are finished, change to state $D4, reduce the body-band limits and clear the twelve-character terrain strip.

Alternate the body's twenty-four colours while the death counter runs. On expiry restore camera/raster hooks, request eleven ordinary actor explosions around the body, clear eight special-weapon flags and award 10000 points. The normal kill flag is requested when it was clear.

Choose a side from the current pose, or a timer bit in the negative action phase. When body Y lies between $42 and $6F, allocate one of four terrain shots on a four-update divider, starting it beside the corresponding side of the body.

For each active two-character shot, restore the prior characters and colours unless a damaging character replaced them. Advance its column by the phase-dependent signed step; out-of-range columns release it. Save the next underlying cells and draw the two shot characters in colour nine. The state and save arrays share nominal map storage at $9A93 onward.
Operand byte 1 of the LDY instruction at $83F3, within the described level actor or raster routine. This name marks a patched operand rather than another routine entry.
Clear the body-band and per-frame flags, put the first band Y into hardware sprites three through six, and publish its preceding scanline as the saved surface coordinate.

Put the first of six shape and colour entries for each of four columns into both screen pointer tables and hardware sprite colours. Install all four X coordinates and merge their high-X bits into the sprite mask.

Display four hardware sprites across successive body bands. Load their current shapes/colours from the column-major matrices, compare the upcoming raster line against the body end, and schedule the next band or cleanup handler. At selected sub-character phases, briefly exchange sprite bitmap rows through $8563.

Select the requested pose, with one pose conditional on player X. Copy twenty-four entries each from the shape, bitmap-low, bitmap-high and colour source arrays into the four-column by six-band live matrices. Save the selected pose index at $BCE8.
Replace two selected shapes, bitmap address bytes and colours in the live pose matrices to produce the flashing body cells.
